items.markdown:
A **pricing strategy** is `the method a business uses to set the price for its products or services, balancing production costs, competitor actions, and customer perceived value`.[[1]](https://www.bdc.ca/en/articles-tools/marketing-sales-export/marketing/pricing-5-common-strategies)[[2]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=hyKOA2gcVi0)

### Common Types of Pricing Strategies

- **Cost-Plus Pricing** : Adds a fixed profit markup directly onto the total cost of production; it is fast and simple, though it ignores customer demand.
- **Competitive Pricing** : Sets prices based on what rivals charge (matching, undercutting, or pricing above them); it works well in crowded markets.
- **Price Skimming** : Launches an innovative or new product at a very high initial price and lowers it over time as competition grows.
- **Penetration Pricing** : Sets a low introductory price to quickly capture market share and attract new customers before raising prices later.
- **Value-Based Pricing** : Prices goods based on how much the target customer believes the product is worth, which is common for luxury or unique brands.
- **Dynamic Pricing** : Adjusts prices in real-time based on shifting market demand, time, or customer location.[[1]](https://www.paddle.com/resources/pricing-strategy)[[2]](https://www.bdc.ca/en/articles-tools/marketing-sales-export/marketing/pricing-5-common-strategies)[[3]](https://www.salesforce.com/sales/revenue-lifecycle-management/pricing-strategies/)[[4]](https://www.coursera.org/articles/pricing-strategy)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pricing_strategy)

### How to Choose the Right Strategy
You can explore comprehensive breakdowns and guides through the [Coursera Pricing Strategy Overview](https://www.coursera.org/articles/pricing-strategy) or the [Salesforce Pricing Strategy Guide](https://www.salesforce.com/sales/revenue-lifecycle-management/pricing-strategies/) . To pick the best option for your business:[[1]](https://www.salesforce.com/sales/revenue-lifecycle-management/pricing-strategies/)[[2]](https://www.coursera.org/articles/pricing-strategy)

1. **Calculate your floor** : Know your exact production and fixed costs so you do not lose money.
2. **Analyze competitors** : Identify 3 to 5 main rivals and see where your product features stand.
3. **Define your value** : Match your price to customer willingness to pay and overall brand positioning.[[1]](https://www.uschamber.com/co/run/finance/pricing-strategies-for-your-business)[[2]](https://www.bdc.ca/en/articles-tools/marketing-sales-export/marketing/pricing-5-common-strategies)[[3]](https://www.salesforce.com/ap/sales/revenue-lifecycle-management/pricing-strategies/)[[4]](https://www.trade.gov/pricing-strategy)[[5]](https://www.paddle.com/resources/pricing-strategy)[[6]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=hyKOA2gcVi0)

If you share **what kind of product or service** you are selling and **who your target customers are** , I can help you pick and test the right pricing model.
